Hi Olga,

We noticed the disruption in Redwood's hosted inference cluster yesterday evening (around 20:10 UTC). Our SOC team asked whether any OptiBank customer data was exposed or lost during the window. Can you confirm whether OptiBank data remained intact and whether there's any evidence of exfiltration?

We'd appreciate a short statement we can share with internal stakeholders and our regulator. Happy to sign an NDA for any attachments if needed.

Thanks,

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-01-10T11:41:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Data integrity confirmation after service interruption

Olga / team — quick ops summary from the forensic scans we ran this morning (attached as a short summary and raw IDs):

Summary findings:
- Scanned all request logs, KV cache access logs, and object-store audit records for the interval 2026-01-09T19:50:00Z to 2026-01-09T21:30:00Z.
- No unauthorized external outbound connections from serving containers were observed. Egress spikes correspond to retries to our internal telemetry endpoint (region us-west-2).
- Object-store read/write events involving OptiBank prefixes show normal patterns; no unexpected reads of keys outside configured model artifacts.
- No signs of data exfiltration or deletion for OptiBank tenant records.

Notes and artifacts:
- Attached: optibank_log_scan_summary.pdf (high-level) and integrity-scanner-raw-ids.csv (list of request IDs and object keys scanned).
- Correlated tracing shows KV cache clear events were triggered by a failing autoscaler job rather than a malicious operation.
- We will keep logs immutable in the evidence folder and have created OPS-1247 to track postmortem evidence collection.

ETA for a polished statement (suitable for regulator): 2026-01-10 EOD PT.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Principal SRE, Incident Response
Redwood Inference

Laura — attaching our formal confirmation per your request. Short summary below; full artifacts attached and a Drive folder link follows.

Summary (for sharing):
- Incident window: 2026-01-09T19:50:00Z — 2026-01-09T21:10:00Z.
- Impact: transient serving degradation affecting a subset of inference instances. No control-plane compromise identified.
- Data integrity: Based on a forensic scan of request logs, KV cache events, and object-store audit logs, Redwood found no evidence of OptiBank customer data deletion, corruption, or exfiltration.
- Actions taken: immutable copies of relevant logs were captured and stored in the OptiBank evidence folder; we've created a Jira ticket (OPS-1247) for long-term retention and regulatory packaging.

Attachments: optibank_log_scan_summary.pdf (high-level findings), integrity-scanner-raw-ids.csv (scanned request/object IDs).
Drive evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/optibank-evidence
Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-1247

If your compliance team needs an NDA-signed copy of the raw logs (CSV), we can provide it — please send the contact and preferred point of contact for the agreement.

Regards,
